claim: Anchor enforces stdlib-only via distro.py AST import scan over product .py files; only third-party allowed is 'winpty' in pty_manager.py (_THIRD_PARTY_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST)
note: A new optional extra (e.g. pywebview) would need a pyproject [project.optional-dependencies] entry + an allowlist entry scoped to one file.

claim: pyproject.toml declares the pywinpty optional extra: terminal = ['pywinpty>=2.0; sys_platform==win32']

Single-instance 8777 guard: _ExclusiveThreadingHTTPServer sets SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE; on EADDRINUSE the duplicate prints 'already running' and sys.exit(0) cleanly (paths.classify_bind_error/use_exclusive_bind)
All desktop launchers (AnchorDashboard.vbs/.bat, launch_anchor.pyw, pin_anchor_to_taskbar.vbs, create_shortcut.py, setup_shortcut.py) ONLY open the browser URL; none spawn a server
anchor_gui.py supports --no-browser and --port; opens webbrowser.open(url) after 0.5s unless --no-browser
NO web manifest or service-worker is served by product code; the only SW code is cache-bust JS that UNREGISTERS all service workers + clears Cache Storage on every load
note: This means Anchor is locked into a no-SW PWA design; offline caching later would require changing this cleanup code.

claim: Favicon/icon routes exist: /favicon.ico->anchor.ico, /anchor.png (256x256), /anchor-touch.png (180x180); brand mark vendor/brand/gwl-m-icon.svg served traversal-safe via brand_asset; .png already in _BRAND_CONTENT_TYPES
No 192x192 or 512x512 PNG exists in the repo; existing PNGs are 256 and 180. The only rasterizer in-repo is PIL in create_shortcut.py, which is third-party and degrades if absent
note: create_shortcut.py is a setup/build script, NOT imported by anchor.py/anchor_gui.py, so it is off the runtime import path; committed PNG bytes do not violate the import scan.

claim: NSSM service `anchor` runs `python anchor_gui.py --no-browser`, binds loopback 127.0.0.1:8777, Automatic start; the UI cannot kill its own server (/api/shutdown removed)

http://localhost and 127.0.0.1 ARE a secure context, so PWA install + service workers work over plain HTTP with no TLS — but ONLY for localhost/127.0.0.1/*.localhost; access by hostname (PUTER/gwl-server) or LAN/Tailscale IP is NOT a secure context and will not install or run a SW
note: Real trap given Anchor's Tailscale/multi-machine context.

claim: A web app manifest ALONE triggers installability in Chromium/Edge since Chrome 108(mobile)/112(desktop); a service worker is NOT required for install (still needed for offline/push, which are moot for an always-on local server)

Recommended manifest fields: name/short_name, icons (192 AND 512 PNG; maskable recommended), start_url, display:standalone, prefer_related_applications:false; a stable `id` pins app identity independent of start_url
note: Caveat: these are RECOMMENDED, not an immutable minimum (Chrome is relaxing criteria). `id` stops same-app reinstall but NOT per-Edge-profile duplicate installs.

claim: An installed Edge PWA on Win11 gives a chromeless standalone window + Start-menu + taskbar + Alt-Tab identity + own icon + 'Add/remove programs' entry
note: Gotchas: install is tied to the Edge profile that created it (won't launch under a different profile — PWABuilder#4886); NOT supported under FSLogix/roaming/RDS. Irrelevant for a single fixed desktop (PUTER) but must be stated. Edge's generic 'Install this site as an app' will appify ANY site but without a manifest may keep chrome/weaker identity.

claim: msedge --app=URL / chrome --app=URL still opens a chromeless window in 2026; it is an unsupported command-line switch with no stability guarantee, and is SEPARATE from the Chrome Apps platform EOL (Oct 2028, ChromeOS-scoped)
note: Appropriately hedged: works today, no contract. --app window groups under Edge's identity, uses default profile unless --user-data-dir (which fragments state).

claim: Edge WebView2 runtime is included as part of Windows 11; pywebview 6.2.1 (Apr 2026) hosts a native window via WebView2 and can point create_window(title, url) at an existing localhost server; pystray-compatible for a system tray
note: Caveat: MS says 'some devices might not have the Runtime pre-installed' and recommends detect-and-install. pywebview/pystray want the main thread — threading design needed.

claim: PyInstaller --onefile self-extracts to temp at runtime -> AV/SmartScreen false positives; Nuitka (compiles to C) trips fewer; unsigned exes get SmartScreen warnings; every recompile resets reputation -> code-signing effectively mandatory
note: Solves 'no Python on the box' — a problem THIS deployment (Python service already running) does not have.

claim: Electron ships its own Chromium+Node (~80-150MB installers); Tauri uses system WebView2 + Rust core (<10MB installers) and can point at an external URL via WebviewUrl::External; both add an entire new toolchain (Node/npm or Rust/cargo)
note: Disproportionate for wrapping a localhost dashboard; if ever a shipped product, Tauri over Electron.

claim: REFUTED-as-trap: the SW-cleanup JS does NOT block PWA install or break an installed PWA (manifest-only PWA uses neither SW registrations nor Cache Storage). 'No SW needed' is safe

AMENDMENT: 'just rasterize the SVG, zero dependency' is wrong — 192/512 PNGs do not exist and stdlib has no SVG rasterizer; producing them needs a third-party tool. Honest form: a one-time OFFLINE build step -> commit PNG bytes as static assets; runtime stays stdlib-only

AMENDMENT: B1 delivers the WINDOW + identity only; the server lifecycle/auto-start is the NSSM service's job (already solved, separate). B1 neither adds nor needs auto-start; a PWA on a down service shows a connection error

AMENDMENT: B2 is NOT strictly dominated by B1 — B2 wins on effort (one-line edit to existing .vbs), zero server-code change, no install gesture, scriptable, and works where Edge install is unavailable. B1 wins on desktop identity. Genuine identity-vs-effort trade-off
CONVERGENCE: both independent reviewers agree the CORE — B1 is technically viable and invariant-safe — survives the adversarial pass; all findings are addressable amendments/caveats, none a BLOCKER
